subproblems.title: A point of the (m+1)-skeleton off the m-skeleton lies on an open unit lattice (m+1)-face (parent step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P). Assume (i) x ∈ L_{m+1}: there is a finite set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s; and (ii) x ∉ L_m: there is no finite set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s. Then x lies on an open unit lattice (m+1)-face. That is, there are a strictly increasing ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P, b ∈ ℤ^P and y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with 0 < y_j < 1 for every j such that x = b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}. In Lean, with p = (ι, b): WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 = x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (x : Euclid P), (∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z) → (¬ ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z) → ∃ (p : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ)) (y : Euclid (m + 1)), StrictMono p.1 ∧ (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ) = x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("L_n ∖ L_m is covered by open faces"; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1), with n = m + 1 and the cardinality and coordinate bookkeeping written out.

Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). For p = (ι, b), Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Coordinate formula, used throughout: Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). In Lean, state it as a local `have` inside the theorem (a leaf may add no separate lemma) and prove it by `simp only [PiLp.add_apply, WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply, PiLp.smul_apply, PiLp.single_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero]`. Plain `simp` gets stuck on `Pi.single`, and EuclideanSpace.single_apply is deprecated in favour of PiLp.single_apply.

1. (Integer coordinates.) Let J := Finset.univ.filter (fun i => ∃ z : ℤ, x_i = z) ⊆ Fin P, so i ∈ J ↔ x_i ∈ ℤ. Work classically, since this predicate is not decidable.
2. (Upper bound on P.) By (i) choose s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s. Then s ⊆ J, so |s| ≤ |J| (Finset.card_le_card) and P ≤ m + 1 + |J|.
3. (Lower bound on P.) If P ≤ m + |J| held, then s := J would satisfy P ≤ m + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s, contradicting (ii). Hence m + |J| < P.
4. (Exactly m + 1 free coordinates.) By steps 2 and 3, P = m + 1 + |J|. So the complement Jᶜ in Fin P has |Jᶜ| = P − |J| = m + 1 (Finset.card_compl, Fintype.card_fin, omega).
5. (Direction map.) Let ι := Jᶜ.orderEmbOfFin h, where h : Jᶜ.card = m + 1 comes from step 4, viewed as a map Fin (m + 1) → Fin P. Then:
   - ι is strictly increasing (OrderEmbedding.strictMono), hence injective;
   - ι(j) ∈ Jᶜ, i.e. ι(j) ∉ J, for every j (Finset.orderEmbOfFin_mem);
   - every i ∉ J equals ι(j) for some j, because range ι = Jᶜ (Finset.range_orderEmbOfFin).
6. (Base point and parameters.) Put b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ (Int.floor) for every i ∈ Fin P, y := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => Int.fract (x_{ι(j)})) ∈ Euclid (m + 1), and p := (ι, b). Thus y_j = Int.fract(x_{ι(j)}).
7. (y lies in the open cube.) Int.fract(x_{ι(j)}) < 1 (Int.fract_lt_one). Since ι(j) ∉ J, x_{ι(j)} is not an integer. In particular x_{ι(j)} ≠ ⌊x_{ι(j)}⌋, so 0 < Int.fract(x_{ι(j)}). (Int.fract_pos is the equivalence 0 < fract a ↔ a ≠ ⌊a⌋; use its .2.) Hence 0 < y_j < 1 for every j.
8. (Φ_p(y) = x, coordinatewise.) Fix i ∈ Fin P. By the coordinate formula, Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ + Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0).
   (a) If i ∈ J, then i ≠ ι(j) for every j (step 5). So every summand is 0 (Finset.sum_eq_zero) and Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋. Write x_i = z with z ∈ ℤ; then ⌊x_i⌋ = ⌊(z : ℝ)⌋ = z = x_i (Int.floor_intCast).
   (b) If i ∉ J, then i = ι(j₀) for some j₀ (step 5). Since ι is injective, the summand for every j ≠ j₀ is 0. So the sum equals y_{j₀} = Int.fract(x_i) (Finset.sum_eq_single), and Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ + Int.fract(x_i) = x_i (Int.floor_add_fract).
   Hence Φ_p(y) = x (PiLp.ext over the coordinates).
9. (Conclusion.) p = (ι, b) and y satisfy all three requirements: StrictMono p.1 (step 5), 0 < y_j < 1 for every j (step 7) and Φ_p(y) = x (step 8). ∎

Lean notes from a compiled scratch proof (≈58 lines as one declaration, the coordinate formula being a local `have`):
- Package J and ι with `obtain`, keeping only their membership and range facts. The witness is p = (⇑ι, fun i => ⌊x i⌋).
- In step 8, rewrite with the coordinate formula (the local `have`) before any `dsimp only`. Running dsimp first unfolds y j to Int.fract …, and the rewrite then fails to match.
- `if_pos`/`if_neg` are deprecated in this toolchain; `ite_eq_left`/`ite_eq_right` work.
proof_key_steps: J := {i : x_i ∈ ℤ}: (i) gives P ≤ m+1+|J|, and (ii) with s := J gives m+|J| < P, so |Jᶜ| = m+1.
ι := orderEmbOfFin of Jᶜ (strictly increasing, range Jᶜ), b := ⌊x⌋, y_j := fract(x_{ι(j)}) ∈ (0,1) because x_{ι(j)} ∉ ℤ.
Coordinatewise Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ = x_i for i ∈ J, and ⌊x_i⌋ + fract(x_i) = x_i for i = ι(j₀); hence Φ_p(y) = x.

subproblems.title: Only finitely many unit lattice faces meet a compact set (parent step 5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. Consider index pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P arbitrary (not necessarily injective) and b ∈ ℤ^P. Only finitely many of them have Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} ∈ K for some y in the closed unit cube [0,1]^k. In Lean, the set {p | ∃ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) 1 ∈ K} is finite.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → {p : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) | ∃ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ) ∈ K}.Finite
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the finiteness part of step 5 of the parent proof (K is compact, so only finitely many faces meet it). The statement allows any ι, not necessarily injective, and the closed cube. So the bound on b below is ⌈ρ⌉ + k rather than the parent's ρ + 1, which relies on ι being injective. Only finiteness is used.

Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). For p = (ι, b), Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, so Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + S_i with S_i := Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). Coordinate formula, used throughout: Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). In Lean, state it as a local `have` inside the theorem (a leaf may add no separate lemma) and prove it by `simp only [PiLp.add_apply, WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply, PiLp.smul_apply, PiLp.single_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero]`. Plain `simp` gets stuck on `Pi.single`, and EuclideanSpace.single_apply is deprecated in favour of PiLp.single_apply.

1. (K is bounded.) K is compact, hence bounded. So there is ρ ∈ ℝ with ‖x‖ ≤ ρ for every x ∈ K (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.exists_norm_le). For every x ∈ ℝ^P and every i, |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
2. (Coordinate shifts.) If y ∈ [0,1]^k, then 0 ≤ S_i ≤ k for every i. Each summand is y_j ∈ [0, 1] or 0, so it lies in [0, 1], and there are k summands (Finset.sum_nonneg, Finset.sum_le_sum, Σ_{j : Fin k} 1 = k).
3. (Bounds on b.) Let p = (ι, b) be in the set, witnessed by y ∈ [0,1]^k with x := Φ_p(y) ∈ K. For each i, |b_i + S_i| = |x_i| ≤ ρ by step 1, so −ρ ≤ b_i + S_i ≤ ρ (abs_le). Put N := ⌈ρ⌉ + k ∈ ℤ. Using ρ ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ (Int.le_ceil), 0 ≤ k and step 2:
   - b_i ≤ ρ − S_i ≤ ρ ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ ≤ N;
   - b_i ≥ −ρ − S_i ≥ −ρ − k ≥ −(⌈ρ⌉ + k) = −N.
   So b_i ∈ [−N, N] for every i; cast the real inequalities back to ℤ (exact_mod_cast). This also works when ρ < 0, for example when K = ∅.
4. (Finiteness.) By step 3 the set is contained in Set.univ ×ˢ (Set.univ.pi fun _ => Set.Icc (−N) N) ⊆ (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ). The first factor is finite (Set.finite_univ; Fin k → Fin P is a Fintype). The second is a finite product of finite integer intervals (Set.Finite.pi, Set.finite_Icc). So the product is finite (Set.Finite.prod), and so is the set (Set.Finite.subset). ∎
proof_key_steps: K compact gives ρ with |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ ≤ ρ on K.
For y ∈ [0,1]^k, Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + S_i with 0 ≤ S_i ≤ k, so |b_i| ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ + k.
The set lies in (all ι) × [−N, N]^P with N = ⌈ρ⌉ + k, which is finite.

Source: steps 8, 10, 11 and 12 of the parent proof restricted to one face p (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, display (33): on an open face, Q₀ is an integer density). The orientation of step 9 is supplied by the sibling child coordinate_plane_orientation_sign (Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfrsd_coordinate_plane_orientation_sign). Its antecedents (IMC-b) and (PO) are those of this statement.

Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, Hⁿ := μHE[n], Φ := Φ_p, Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, F̆ := Φ(Q₁), c := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)), E_p := (j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1), vol := volume on Euclid n.

1. (Measurability.)
   - Q₁ = ⋂_i ({y : 0 < y_i} ∩ {y : y_i < 1}) is Borel (measurableSet_lt with the continuous coordinate maps y ↦ y_i, by fun_prop).
   - Φ is an isometry, hence a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding) and therefore a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding).
   - So F̆ = Φ(Q₁) is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image, an iff; use .2), and so is M ∩ F̆.
2. (F̆ lies in a coordinate plane.) Let a = Φ(y) and let i be an index with ι(j) ≠ i for all j. Then a_i = b_i + Σ_j y_j·(e_{ι(j)})_i = b_i = c_i. In Lean: rintro a ⟨y, -, rfl⟩ i hi; simp [Ne.symm (hi _)].
3. (Orientation sign.) Apply the sibling coordinate_plane_orientation_sign to (IMC-b), (PO), P, n, U := univ (isOpen_univ), R, ι, c and E := F̆, using StrictMono ι, step 1 and step 2. It gives a measurable σ : ℝ^P → ℤ with |σ(x)| ≤ 1 for every x such that, for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ F̆)-a.e. x, ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(E_p) for every n-covector α.
4. (Change of variables.)
   - Hⁿ on Euclid n equals vol (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
   - Φ is an isometry, so Measure.map Φ Hⁿ = Hⁿ⌞range Φ (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure).
   - Since F̆ ⊆ range Φ and Φ⁻¹(F̆) = Q₁ (Function.Injective.preimage_image): Hⁿ⌞F̆ = (Hⁿ⌞range Φ)⌞F̆ = (map Φ vol)⌞F̆ = map Φ (vol⌞Q₁) (Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map).
   Hence ∫_{F̆} f dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} f(Φ(y)) dy for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). Likewise ∫⁻_{F̆} f dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{Q₁} f(Φ(y)) dy for every f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). Neither identity needs f to be measurable or integrable. When rewriting, pass the integrand explicitly, e.g. (fun x => g x * ω x E_p); higher-order unification fails otherwise.
5. (The density.) Let g := M.indicator (x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ)·(σ(x) : ℝ)), θ' := M.indicator (x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞])), and u(y) := g(Φ(y)).
   (a) g is Borel: θ and σ are measurable, every map out of ℕ or ℤ is measurable (Measurable.of_discrete), products of measurable maps are measurable, and M is Borel (Measurable.indicator). Φ is continuous, so u is Borel.
   (b) u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y: if Φ(y) ∈ M then u(y) = θ(Φ y)·σ(Φ y) with integer factors, and otherwise u(y) = 0.
   (c) ofReal|g(x)| ≤ θ'(x) for every x. For x ∈ M, |θ(x)σ(x)| = θ(x)|σ(x)| ≤ θ(x), since θ(x) ≥ 0 and |σ(x)| ≤ 1. For x ∉ M both sides are 0.
6. (Face mass.) R.measure(F̆) = ((Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ)(F̆) = (Hⁿ.withDensity θ')(F̆) = ∫⁻_{F̆} θ' dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{Q₁} θ'(Φ(y)) dy. The lemmas used are, in order: IMRep.measure, withDensity_indicator (M Borel), withDensity_apply (F̆ Borel), and step 4.
7. (Finiteness.) C := WithLp.toLp 2 '' (Set.univ.pi fun _ => Set.Icc 0 1) is compact (isCompact_univ_pi, isCompact_Icc, continuity of WithLp.toLp) and contains Q₁; for y ∈ Q₁ the preimage point is WithLp.ofLp y, and toLp (ofLp y) = y by rfl. K := Φ(C) is compact (Φ is continuous) and contains F̆. So R.measure(F̆) ≤ R.measure(K) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. Here the equality is withDensity_apply plus Measure.restrict_restrict, and finiteness is R.locallyIntegrable_mult K applied with K ⊆ univ.
8. (Integrability and the mass bound.)
   - By 5(c) and step 6, ∫⁻_{Q₁} ofReal|u(y)| dy ≤ ∫⁻_{Q₁} θ'(Φ(y)) dy = R.measure(F̆), which is < ∞ by step 7.
   - With 5(a), u is integrable on Q₁ (hasFiniteIntegral_iff_enorm, Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs).
   - Then |u| is integrable on Q₁ and nonnegative, so ofReal(∫_{Q₁}|u|) = ∫⁻_{Q₁} ofReal|u| ≤ R.measure(F̆) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal).
9. (The integral identity.) Fix a test form ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n and write ω_p(x) := ω(x)(E_p).
   (a) For Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ F̆)-a.e. x, step 3 holds and x ∈ M ∩ F̆ (ae_restrict_mem). For such x, θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = θ(x)·σ(x)·ω_p(x) = g(x)·ω_p(x), because g(x) = θ(x)σ(x) for x ∈ M. Hence ∫_{M ∩ F̆} θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{M ∩ F̆} g·ω_p dHⁿ (integral_congr_ae).
   (b) g·ω_p vanishes on F̆ ∖ (M ∩ F̆), because g = 0 off M. Since F̆ is Borel and M ∩ F̆ ⊆ F̆, ∫_{M ∩ F̆} g·ω_p dHⁿ = ∫_{F̆} g·ω_p dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero; the older ..._forall_diff_eq_zero is a deprecated alias).
   (c) By step 4, ∫_{F̆} g·ω_p dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} g(Φ(y))·ω(Φ(y))(E_p) dy = ∫_{Q₁} u(y)·ω(Φ(y))(E_p) dy.
10. (Conclusion.) u meets all four requirements: integer values everywhere (5(b)); integrability on Q₁ and ofReal(∫_{Q₁}|u|) ≤ R.measure(F̆) (step 8); and the integral identity for every ω (step 9). ∎

2. Countable reduction. ℝ^P is second countable, so ⋃𝒲 = ⋃_k W_k for a countable subfamily (W_k) ⊆ 𝒲 (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable). By countable subadditivity it suffices to show H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 for one fixed W ∈ 𝒲.
3. A finite measure. C := closure W is compact and C ⊆ U, so ∫_{M ∩ C} θ dH^n < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞. Put ν := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C), a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
4. Orientation facts. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a plane Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, s ∈ {1, −1}. At such x: (a) |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm of the continuous alternating map, since |τ_i| = 1); (b) ξ(x) ≠ 0: the n-covector β_τ(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b} (for n = 0 the constant 1) is continuous, multilinear and alternating, and β_τ(τ) = det I = 1, so ξ(x)(β_τ) = s ≠ 0.
5. Testing T. Fix an n-covector α and set f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α). It is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for μ ≥ ν) and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ ν-a.e., so f_α ∈ L¹(ν). For every g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P, ℝ) with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω(x) := g(x)·α is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in W. As T vanishes on W and R represents T: 0 = T ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(g(x)α) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν (the integrand vanishes off W ⊆ C).
6. Fundamental lemma. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (open set W, measure ν, f_α locally integrable on W) gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M and ν is carried by M, ξ(x)(α) = 0 for ν-a.e. x ∈ W.
7. Conclusion. Let α_1, …, α_m be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P. Intersecting the finitely many full-measure sets of step 6, for ν-a.e. x ∈ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, hence ξ(x) = 0. By step 4(b), ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x. Therefore ν(W) = H^n(M ∩ C ∩ W) = H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, and by step 2, H^n(M ∖ T.support) = 0.

Testing T with g·α (g ∈ C_c^∞(W), α a constant covector) gives ∫ g θ ξ(α) dH^n⌞M = 0.
The fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations gives ξ = 0 a.e. on M ∩ W, while unit orientations are nonzero; hence H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.

Source: parent proof step 1 ('For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C, ξ(x) = ±ev_τ with τ orthonormal, so |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for all α. Hence for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the functions θ ξ(ω) … are bounded a.e. on C by θ ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω} … and are integrable on C'). This makes explicit the absolute convergence of the integral in Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (‡) (chapter-06.txt lines 733–745), where θ is locally Hⁿ-integrable and ξ = τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ with τ orthonormal.

Notation: μ := μHE[n], C := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, f := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n), K := tsupport f, and F(x) := (θ(x) : ℝ)·ξ(x)(f(x)).

1. (Test-form data.) ω ∈ TestFormOn U n means IsTestForm f ∧ tsupport f ⊆ U (ω.2.1 and ω.2.2). IsTestForm f means ContDiff ℝ ∞ f and HasCompactSupport f. Hence:
   - f is continuous;
   - K is compact and closed, hence measurable, and K ⊆ U;
   - f(x) = 0 for x ∉ K (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
   By Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support there is B ∈ ℝ with ‖f(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. Here ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n = (Euclid P) [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ.

2. (Pointwise bound for ξ.) By the field R.orients, for μ⌞C-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with Orthonormal ℝ τ such that either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all n-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
   - For every α, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm gives ‖α(τ)‖ ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖.
   - ∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = 1, since ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for each i (first component of Orthonormal). For n = 0 the product is empty and equals 1.
   - Hence |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ for all α (use abs_neg in the second case).
   So for μ⌞C-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every α.

3. (Measurability.)
   - x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable: θ is measurable and every function on ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat composed with R.measurable_mult).
   - The evaluation map MultiVector P n × Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ, (φ, α) ↦ φ(α), is continuous (Continuous.clm_apply applied to continuous_fst and continuous_snd).
   - x ↦ (ξ(x), f(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞C: pair R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient with the continuous f using AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk.
   - Hence x ↦ ξ(x)(f(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable), and so is F (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).
   Formalization note: applying ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ to ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ fails to unify the topology instance on MultiVector P n. Composing with the continuous evaluation map, as above, works.

4. (Integrable dominating function.) Let g(x) := B * K.indicator (fun x => (θ x : ℝ)) x, i.e. g = B·1_K·θ.
   - x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is integrable on K for μ⌞C. It is measurable by step 3. Its lower integral is ∫⁻_K ‖(θ(x) : ℝ)‖ₑ d(μ⌞C) = ∫⁻_{K∩C} θ dμ = ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ dμ, using Measure.restrict_restrict (K measurable) and ‖(k : ℝ)‖ₑ = (k : ℝ≥0∞) for k ∈ ℕ (hasFiniteIntegral_iff_enorm).
   - This lower integral is ≠ ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult K, since K is compact and K ⊆ U.
   - Hence K.indicator θ is integrable for μ⌞C (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator, K measurable), and so is g (Integrable.const_mul).

5. (Domination.) Let x be one of the a.e. points of step 2.
   - If x ∈ K: |F(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(f(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖f(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·B = g(x), using θ(x) ≥ 0, step 2 and step 1.
   - If x ∉ K: f(x) = 0, so F(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0 = g(x).
   Thus ‖F(x)‖ ≤ g(x) for μ⌞C-a.e. x.

6. (Conclusion.) Integrable.mono' applies: g is integrable (step 4), F is a.e. strongly measurable (step 3), and the a.e. bound holds (step 5). Hence F is integrable for μ⌞C = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω is continuous with compact support K = tsupport ω ⊆ U, so ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B everywhere and ω = 0 off K.
R.orients gives ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) with τ orthonormal a.e. on C, so |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ by le_opNorm and ∏‖τ_i‖ = 1.
The integrand is a.e. strongly measurable: compose the continuous evaluation map with (ξ, ω).
It is dominated a.e. by B·1_K·θ, which is integrable because ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult).
Integrable.mono' concludes.
